summary: Modified pi-global-resources.ts to add a helper that filters out Pi extensions declaring `"runtime": "tui"` in a sidecar metadata file, then added tests for the new behavior. Afterwards the conversation pivoted to scouting two upstream skill repositories (cursor/plugins pstack and mattpocock/skills) to design a Gizmo adapter registry that vendors them as no-op Pi extensions, with pinned snapshots, curated inclusion, and individual skill opt-in.
decisions: Pi extensions that only provide TUI extensions with no other Gizmo integration are excluded from Gizmo by checking a sidecar metadata file for `"runtime": "tui"` (chosen over an empty-integration load-all approach, after user selected 'Explicit compatibility metadata' as the filter mechanism).
A new adapter registry is recommended rather than treating either upstream repository directly as a Gizmo registry, because neither follows Gizmo's gizmo.registry.json extension layout.
Upstream skill content should be vendored as pinned snapshots with recorded commits and refreshed via reviewable update PRs, not downloaded mutably at install time.
Each adapter package is a no-op Pi extension with a `gizmoExtension` id/name export and a package manifest pointing Pi to a `skills/` directory, letting Pi discover nested SKILL.md files recursively.

pstack should initially publish a curated Pi-compatible subset (general engineering principles, TypeScript/TDD/writing/architecture/review skills) rather than the whole repository, because much of pstack assumes Cursor-specific model names, subagent types, and orchestration features.
Individual skills within each package should be disabled by default so users can opt in, rather than enabling whole collections automatically.
errors: Read of apps/agent-server/tests/resources/pi-global-resources.test.ts initially failed with ENOENT; resolved by listing the directory and creating the new test file.
